name: Goblet Squat
summary: A beginner-friendly squat where a dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest acts as a counterweight, making it easy to sit upright and learn good squat mechanics.
setup: Hold one end of a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, or hold a kettlebell by the horns.
Keep your elbows pointing down and close to the ribs.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes turned out a little.
Brace your trunk and keep the weight against your chest.
execution: Push your hips back and bend your knees to sit down between your legs.
Keep your chest up and let your elbows move inside your knees at the bottom.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as deep as you can with a neutral spine.
Press through the whole foot to stand up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Keep the weight against your chest for the entire set.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbell drift away from the body and the torso fold forward: keep it pinned to your chest and elbows down.
Knees collapsing inward: push the knees out in line with the toes, using the elbows as a cue.
Heels lifting: place your weight on the midfoot and heel and widen the stance a bit.
Using a weight that is too heavy to hold: pick a load you can keep tight against the chest for all reps.
